title: A .env file does nothing until someone reads it
subtitle: Either Node reads it before the app starts, or the app reads it itself. Either way the lines end up in process.env.

nodes.label: .env
nodes.detail:
a plain text file
NAME=Tanvi
COLOR=pink

nodes.label: Way 1: Node reads it
nodes.detail:
node --env-file=.env app.js
before app.js even starts
app.js doesn't know about the file

nodes.label: Way 2: app.js reads it
nodes.detail:
process.loadEnvFile()  (or dotenv)
at the top of app.js
then plain: node app.js

nodes.label: Nobody reads it
nodes.detail:
plain node app.js
with the old app.js

nodes.label: localhost:3000
nodes.detail:
white page
Hello, friend!
(the defaults in app.js)

notes.text:
The file only fills in what's missing.

COLOR=green node app.js → green page. A setting that's already in the environment always beats the file.

node app.js                    # old app.js: Hello, friend! (white)
node --env-file=.env app.js    # Way 1: Hello, Tanvi! (pink)
node app.js                    # Way 2, app.js has loadEnvFile(): Hello, Tanvi! (pink)
COLOR=green node app.js        # real setting wins: Hello, Tanvi! (green)
